record.original_question: For the d-dimensional hypercube Q_d, does there exist an absolute integer constant c such that every strong orientation of Q_d contains a directed cycle of length at most c? In other words, can one bound the length of the shortest directed cycle in every strongly connected orientation of every hypercube by a constant independent of d?

evidence.quote: Does There exist an integer c such that for every d ∈ N, every strong orientation of Qd, the hypercube of dimension d, has a directed cycle of lenght ≤ c ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d \ge 1$, let $Q_d$ denote the $d$-dimensional hypercube graph: its vertex set is $\{0,1\}^d$, and two vertices are adjacent if and only if they differ in exactly one coordinate. An orientation of $Q_d$ is an assignment of a direction to each edge, producing a directed graph; it is called a strong orientation if the resulting digraph is strongly connected (i.e., for any ordered pair of vertices $u,v$ there is a directed path from $u$ to $v$). A directed cycle of length $\ell$ in an oriented graph is a sequence $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_{\ell-1}, v_\ell = v_0$ of distinct vertices (except $v_0 = v_\ell$) such that each $(v_i, v_{i+1})$ is a directed edge.

Question: Does there exist an absolute integer constant $c$, independent of $d$, such that for every $d \ge 2$ and every strong orientation of $Q_d$, the resulting digraph contains a directed cycle of length at most $c$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published resolution of the question of whether the shortest directed cycle in every strong orientation of $Q_d$ can be bounded by a constant independent of $d$. Related literature treats undirected cycles in hypercubes, strong orientations of general graphs (Robbins' theorem), and directed girth in digraphs with minimum out-degree conditions, but none of the retrieved sources answer this specific question. The status appears to be open, but this could not be confirmed authoritatively.

status_evidence.title: Strong orientation - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A strong orientation of an undirected graph is an assignment of a direction to each edge that makes it into a strongly connected graph; by Robbins' theorem these exist exactly for bridgeless graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background on strong orientations but does not address the constant-girth question for hypercubes.

status_evidence.title: Hypercube graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General reference on $Q_d$, its girth (4 for $d \ge 2$), and Hamiltonicity properties.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference on hypercubes; does not resolve directed-girth bounds for strong orientations.

status_evidence.title: Short cycles in directed graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Every directed graph with n vertices and minimum out-degree k contains a directed cycle of length at most n/k + O(1).
status_evidence.claim: Generic bounds on directed girth do not yield a constant bound for strong orientations of $Q_d$.
